headline: UK officials have not committed to adding AI-specific safeguards to the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill, saying only that amendments are under consideration.
score_reason: Reported from an on-the-record parliamentary hearing; no decision yet, so watchlist.
importance_line: It affects how soon the UK gets binding rules against AI-driven cyber threats, such as the self-replicating worms Anthropic warned could be months away, though Anthropic's forecast is an extrapolation and the government has only said it is "looking at" changes.
summary: The Register reports that senior civil servants told MPs this week the government is still considering amendments to the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill to address AI risks, even though AI minister Kanishka Narayan has promised to "legislate wherever necessary". Committee chair Liam Byrne replied that "you have to legislate for something in a bill", not merely consider it.
notes: Hearing was Tuesday 13 Oct 2026; Register published 15 Oct.
